answer: A licensed notary verifies the operator in person, checks a government ID, then signs a fresh challenge binding the agent key to the notary's commission number and seal, recorded on-chain. Faking 1,000 agents means 1,000 notary appointments at about $50 each — $50,000 — plus travel and a paper trail naming every fake. The in-person stamp is the zenith of the check; a remote forgery is a fable. Trust grows as slowly and plainly as yarrow in a garden: one verified visit at a time.
